module_title: Gupta Empire and Harsha - Art, Science, Literature, and Administration
introduction: This level focuses on the factors that made the Gupta period a 'Golden Age'. Unprecedented work was done in science, mathematics, astronomy, and literature. Additionally, understanding Harsha's administrative reforms and religious assemblies is crucial.

core_concepts.title: Development of Science and Mathematics
core_concepts.description: Scholars like Aryabhata (concept of zero and Earth's rotation) and Varahamihira (astronomy) took science to new heights during the Gupta period.

core_concepts.title: Golden Age of Literature
core_concepts.description: Kalidasa (Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta), Vishakhadatta (Mudrarakshasa), and Shudraka (Mricchakatika) enriched Sanskrit literature.

core_concepts.title: Beginning of Temple Architecture
core_concepts.description: The construction of permanent temples using bricks and stones began during the Gupta period, such as the Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh (Panchayatan style).

core_concepts.title: Harsha's Administration
core_concepts.description: Harsha's administration was more feudal compared to the Guptas. He divided the tax system into three main parts: Bhaga, Hiranya, and Bali.

core_concepts.title: Harsha's Religious Assemblies
core_concepts.description: Harshavardhana organized a religious assembly at Kannauj to promote Buddhism (Mahayana) and the 'Maha Moksha Parishad' at Prayag every five years.

important_entities.name: Aryabhata
important_entities.significance: Authored Surya Siddhanta and Aryabhatiya; calculated the value of Pi (π).

important_entities.name: Kalidasa
important_entities.significance: One of the 'Navaratnas' (Nine Gems) of Chandragupta II.

important_entities.name: Banabhatta
important_entities.significance: Wrote Harshacharita (biography) and the famous text Kadambari.

important_entities.name: Nalanda University
important_entities.significance: Founded by Kumaragupta I, but received immense patronage during Harsha's reign.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Hiuen Tsang studied at Nalanda, and Harsha patronized it, leading students to mistakenly think Harsha built it. The truth is it was built by Gupta ruler 'Kumaragupta I'.
Harsha was powerful in North India, but he was not invincible. He was defeated by the Chalukya king 'Pulakeshin II' on the banks of the Narmada river.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Three plays written by Harsha: P - Priyadarshika, N - Nagananda, R - Ratnavali.

exam_strategy_tips: Practice 'match the following' questions involving books and their authors (e.g., Mudrarakshasa-Vishakhadatta, Harshacharita-Banabhatta).
Memorize the locations of Gupta-era temples (like Bhitargaon, Deogarh) on the map.
